text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
- The government has reached an agreement with the Vatican on financing of the Roman Catholic Church in Hungary and resolution of its property claims.

- Socialist parliamentary group leader Imre Szekeres told reporters Thursday that efforts to prevent a deterioration in the economy and halt the impoverishment of society have been successful, while sustainable growth has begun.
- The central budget deficit rose by 13.6 billion forints to 126.7 billion in April, in line with expectations, Finance Ministry deputy state secretary Csaba Laszlo told reporters Thursday.
- The operation of three home savings funds was okayed yesterday by the State Capital Supervision. Fundamenta Rt., Lakaskassza Rt. and the OTP Home Savings Rt. will open their gates next week.

- Senior officials of the Socialist Party and opposition Smallholders have made it known, couched in cautiously worded statements, that a coalition government between the two parties has not been ruled out following the 1998 elections.
- Russia is scheduled to repay half of its outstanding $600 million state debt to Hungary this year, and the other half before the turn of the millennium, experts agreed in Moscow Thursday.
- Industrial production in March stayed 8.6 percent below that of the previous month, but was 3.3 percent higher than in March 1996, the Central Statistics Office (KSH) reports.
- About 40% of the 3,296 retail managers interviewed by the economic research firm Kopint-Datorg in March expect their companies' revenues to increase in the second quarter.

- The annual general meeting of plastics manufacturer Pannonplast Rt. approved the company's 1996 results Thursday. Sales revenues amounted to 9.7 billion forints, up from 8.2 billion forints in 1995.
- Pre-tax profits at OTP Bank Rt. in the first three months of 1997 rose by 38 percent over the first quarter of last year to 4.66 billion forints, the bank reported yesterday.
- Six men were arrested yesterday for kidnapping an acquaintance and demanding a ransom of one million forints $5,538).
